# The service levels in Kestrel's contract with Brannock City Transport.
# The shape follows the service levels in Citi Bike's monthly report to New York City:
# https://mot-marketing-whitelabel-prod.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/nyc/April-2026-Citi-Bike-Monthly-Report.pdf
# Nobody edits this file except the city. Claude Code must never change it.
contract: Brannock City Transport and Kestrel Bike Share
service_levels:
  - id: SLA-4
    name: Bike defects
    rule: A rider pressing the wrench button is notice of a defect.
    clock_starts: when the rider reports the defect (the wrench)
    wrenched_limit_hours: 48
    not_wrenched_limit_hours: 96
    target_percent: 95
    credit_per_late_bike_gbp: 50
  - id: SLA-9
    name: Bike availability
    rule: The share of the fleet that riders can rent, across every district.
    minimum_percent: 96
  - id: SLA-11
    name: Station outage
    rule: No single station outage lasts longer than this.
    limit_hours: 4
  - id: SLA-12
    name: Public feed accuracy
    rule: Real-time data in the public feed is accurate and available to the public at all times.
    feed_max_age_seconds: 60

# Release notes: broken bikes leave the map, and crews fix the most urgent first

## Riders

- When you report a broken bike, we take it off the list of bikes you can rent.
- This happens within one minute.
- The station count shows one less bike ready to ride, so you will not walk to a bike that does not work.
- Our crews now fix the most urgent bikes first, so the bikes you report get fixed faster.
- Thank you for telling us about broken bikes. Every report helps keep riders safe.

## Crews

- The crew queue now puts the job that is due first on top. When two jobs are due at the same time, the older job comes first.
- The 48 hour clock starts when the rider reports the bike, not when the job is opened.
- A reported bike is taken out of service at the same moment its repair job is created.

# Rollout plan: broken bikes leave the map, and crews fix the most urgent first.
# See work/release.md. The release manager approves this file before deploy:production.
# Thresholds come only from data/contract/sla.yaml.

# Proposed name. No feature flag exists in src/ yet; P-items must add it before rollout.
feature_flag: wrench_takes_bike_out_of_service

# District names from data/stations.csv.
stages:
  - districts: [North]           # 40 stations
  - districts: [Centre]          # 40 stations
  - districts: [East, West]      # 30 + 35 stations
  - districts: [South]           # 35 stations

guardrails:
  - metric: fleet_rentable_percent             # share of fleet riders can rent, across every district
    stop_below: 96                             # SLA-9 minimum_percent
  - metric: public_feed_age_seconds            # age of real-time data in the public feed
    stop_above: 60                             # SLA-12 feed_max_age_seconds
  - metric: wrenched_bikes_fixed_in_48h_percent  # clock starts at the wrench, not when dispatch opens the job
    stop_below: 95                             # SLA-4 target_percent (within wrenched_limit_hours: 48)
  - metric: longest_station_outage_hours
    stop_above: 4                              # SLA-11 limit_hours

rollback:
  command: bun run rollback
  when: >-
    Any guardrail crosses its threshold in a district that has the flag on,
    or the public feed stops serving. Run it first, then turn the flag off and
    tell the release manager. Do not move to the next stage until every
    guardrail holds in the current stage.

I wrote `work/rollout.yaml`, and one part of it needs a decision from you: **the feature flag doesn't exist yet.** I searched `src/`, `scripts/` and `work/` and found no flag or toggle, so `wrench_takes_bike_out_of_service` is a name I made up. Either rename it or add a plan item that builds it before the rollout.

**Stages** use the district names in `data/stations.csv`:
1. North (40 stations)
2. Centre (40)
3. East and West together (30 + 35)
4. South (35)

**Guardrails.** Every number comes from `data/contract/sla.yaml`, and each line has a comment naming its SLA id:

| Metric | Stop when | Source |
|---|---|---|
| `fleet_rentable_percent` | below 96 | SLA-9 `minimum_percent` |
| `public_feed_age_seconds` | above 60 | SLA-12 `feed_max_age_seconds` |
| `wrenched_bikes_fixed_in_48h_percent` | below 95 | SLA-4 `target_percent` (the 48 hours count from the wrench) |
| `longest_station_outage_hours` | above 4 | SLA-11 `limit_hours` |

The metric names are mine, since the contract doesn't name any. I didn't use SLA-4's 96-hour limit for bikes that weren't wrenched or its £50 credit as guardrails.

**Rollback:** the command is `bun run rollback`, which is in `package.json`. Run it when any guardrail crosses its threshold in a district that has the flag on, or when the public feed stops serving. After that, turn the flag off and tell the release manager. The next stage starts only when every guardrail holds in the current one.

I didn't run `bun test` because the command needed approval. The only change is this YAML file, which no code reads. I haven't run `bun run approve` or deployed; the release manager still has to approve the file.
